title: Source tax: residence abroad and cross-border questions
purpose: Derive the calculator's residence answer from the home address. Germany residents are asked the cross-border questions (daily return, certificate of residence, reasonable return, more than 60 non-return days), which decide the cross-border tariff. Liechtenstein residents are asked about daily return and more than 45 non-return days, which can lead to 'in principle no source tax liability' flagged for HR.

stories.title: Derive the calculator's residence answers from the home address
stories.i_want: Lonio to derive the source tax calculator's residence answers (main residence in Switzerland, and otherwise Germany, Liechtenstein or another country) from the country of the employee's home address, without asking the employee a separate residence question
stories.so_that: the employee is asked where they live only once. Lonio can then pick the right cross-border follow-up questions and compute the tariff code, and I no longer have to work through the calculator's residence block by hand
stories.priority_reason: Every other residence-dependent question and the computed tariff code (D-001) depend on this. HR finds the questions for employees living abroad hard to keep track of today (F-hr_transcript-8595fb).

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence for source tax is derived from the country of the home address
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has entered the country of their home address (the address is asked of everyone and owned by the address section)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the residence answer that the source tax calculator would ask for
acceptance_criteria.then: The residence is 'Switzerland' if the country is Switzerland, 'Germany' if it is Germany, 'Liechtenstein' if it is Liechtenstein, and 'Other country' for any other country. The employee is not asked a separate residence or country-of-residence question for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Switzerland and other countries get no cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee lives in Switzerland or in a country other than Germany or Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the source tax part of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: None of the Germany questions (daily return, certificate of residence, reasonable return, more than 60 non-return days) and none of the Liechtenstein questions (daily return, more than 45 non-return days) are asked. The tariff code is computed from the base tariff, as in the calculator.

acceptance_criteria.title: Changing the country of residence removes the cross-border answers on submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee answered the Germany or Liechtenstein questions and then changes the country of their home address to another country
acceptance_criteria.then: Answers to cross-border questions that no longer apply are not kept. Until submission they may be kept, so that going back and forth loses no input.

stories.title: Germany: daily return and certificate of residence
stories.i_want: employees living in Germany to be asked whether they return daily to their main residence in Germany and, if they do, whether they have handed in a certificate of residence
stories.so_that: the cross-border (Grenzgänger) tariff is applied only when the calculator's conditions are met, and the normal tariff is applied otherwise
stories.priority_reason: Without these answers Lonio cannot compute the tariff code for employees living in Germany (D-001). HR cannot remember these questions today (F-hr_transcript-8595fb).

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return to Germany is asked only of employees living in Germany
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is subject to source tax (everyone living abroad is)
acceptance_criteria.when: the country of their home address is Germany
acceptance_criteria.then: The employee is asked whether they return daily to their main residence in Germany, answered 'yes' or 'no'. The answer is required. Employees living in any other country are not asked. The answer is recorded for source tax (the cross-border tariff decision).

acceptance_criteria.title: Certificate of residence is asked only after a daily return
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer that they return daily to their main residence in Germany
acceptance_criteria.then: They are asked whether they have handed in a certificate of residence, answered 'yes', 'no' or 'not yet'. The answer is required. Employees who do not return daily are not asked. The certificate itself goes to HR outside Lonio; nothing is uploaded.

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return with a certificate gives the cross-border tariff; without one, the normal tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany who is subject to source tax returns daily to their main residence in Germany
acceptance_criteria.then: If the certificate of residence has been handed in ('yes'), the cross-border tariff applies. If the answer is 'no' or 'not yet', the normal tariff applies. Employees living outside Germany always get the normal tariff from this rule. The cross-border result changes the tariff letter (A to L, B to M, C to N, H to P; see the tariff letter rule). The A/B/H paths are verified before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.title: A certificate handed in later is reflected in the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee answered 'not yet' for the certificate of residence and submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the answer is later changed to 'yes' (a change made by HR, specified in the later HR-side spec)
acceptance_criteria.then: The cross-border tariff decision and the tariff code are derived again from the latest answers. The employee cannot change the answer after submission.

examples.name: Certificate later recorded as handed in

stories.title: Germany: no daily return - reasonableness and more than 60 non-return days
stories.i_want: employees living in Germany who do not return daily to be asked whether a daily return would basically be reasonable (less than 100 km driving distance) and, if so, whether they expect more than 60 work-related non-return days in the calendar year
stories.so_that: the cross-border tariff or the normal tariff is applied as the calculator would apply it
stories.priority_reason: Without these answers Lonio cannot compute the tariff code for Germany residents who do not return daily (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Reasonableness of a daily return is asked only when the employee does not return daily
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany is subject to source tax (everyone living abroad is)
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer that they do not return daily to their main residence in Germany
acceptance_criteria.then: They are asked whether a daily return would basically be reasonable (less than 100 km driving distance), answered 'yes' or 'no'. The answer is required. Employees who return daily, or who live outside Germany, are not asked. The answer is recorded for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: More than 60 non-return days is asked only when a daily return is reasonable
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany who is subject to source tax does not return daily
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer that a daily return would be reasonable
acceptance_criteria.then: They are asked whether they expect more than 60 work-related non-return days in the calendar year, answered 'yes' or 'no'. The answer is required. The employee states what they expect for the year; no proof is collected in Lonio. If a daily return is not reasonable, the question is not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Tariff decision for Germany residents who do not return daily
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany who is subject to source tax does not return daily
acceptance_criteria.then: If a daily return is not reasonable, the normal tariff applies. If it is reasonable and the employee expects more than 60 non-return days, the normal tariff applies. If it is reasonable and they do not expect more than 60, the cross-border tariff applies, which changes the tariff letter (see the tariff letter rule). The A/B/H paths are verified before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

stories.title: Liechtenstein: daily return and more than 45 non-return days
stories.i_want: employees living in Liechtenstein to be asked whether they return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein and, if not, whether they expect more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year
stories.so_that: Lonio records, as the calculator would, either 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' (flagged for me) or the normal tariff code
stories.priority_reason: HR names Liechtenstein residents among the employees living abroad (F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a). Without these answers there is no source tax result for them (D-001, D-007).

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return to Liechtenstein is asked only of employees living in Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee lives in Liechtenstein and therefore counts as subject to source tax, so they are asked the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the residence questions for source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: They are asked whether they return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein, answered 'yes' or 'no'. The answer is required. Employees living in any other country are not asked. The answer is recorded for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: More than 45 non-return days is asked only when the employee does not return daily
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Liechtenstein is asked the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer that they do not return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.then: They are asked whether they expect more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year, answered 'yes' or 'no'. The answer is required. The employee states what they expect for the year; no proof is collected in Lonio. Employees who return daily are not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: 'In principle no source tax liability' or the normal tariff code for Liechtenstein residents
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Liechtenstein has answered the Liechtenstein questions
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the source tax result
acceptance_criteria.then: If the employee returns daily, or does not return daily and expects at most 45 non-return days, the result is 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code, and it is recorded for HR as a flag. If they expect more than 45 non-return days, the normal tariff code applies. For employees living outside Liechtenstein the rule does not apply and the tariff code is computed as usual. How HR sees and handles the flag is part of the later HR-side spec.
